course.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence for DevOps
course.subtitle: The AI words and ideas every DevOps engineer needs, and a real 3 a.m. outage fixed by hand and then with an AI helper. Free, about 90 minutes.
course.description:
AI is in every DevOps conversation, and so is the confusion. This free course gives you the foundation in about 90 minutes: what AI is, the words you will hear every day, and what actually changes when an AI helper joins an engineer on call.

## What you'll build
- **A 3 a.m. outage, fixed twice:** first the classic way with logs, config and a runbook, then with an AI helper on Amazon Bedrock. Both come with a hands-on lab, so you can run them yourself.
- **A side-by-side demo** of the same model working as a chatbot and as an agent, so the difference is obvious.

## Why this course
- **Short and focused:** twelve lessons, each one idea, each starting from an everyday example.
- **Made for engineers:** every word is mapped to systems you already run, from pipelines to on-call.
- **Quizzes with the answers explained** after the lessons, so you know what stuck.
- **A clear next step:** when you finish, the AWS and Azure masterclasses take you from these foundations to building and running AI systems.

## Who it's for
DevOps, cloud and software engineers and IT professionals with little or no AI experience.
objectives: Explain AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI, and how they differ from rule-based software
Use the core vocabulary correctly: models, tokens, context windows, temperature, hallucinations and embeddings
Describe what changes when an AI helper joins an on-call engineer, and what the engineer must still check
Tell an AI chatbot from an AI agent, and explain tools, the agent loop, memory and guardrails
Explain what the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is and why AI platforms adopted it
Choose your next step: the AI for DevOps masterclass on AWS or on Azure
requirements: Basic familiarity with IT or software work
Optional: Docker on your computer for the two outage labs

sections.title: What AI is, and what it changes for DevOps

lessons.title: How computers solved problems before AI
lessons.summary: See how rule-based programs work, why most of the software you run still works that way, and where hand-written rules break down: everyday language, images and cases nobody planned for.

lessons.title: What machine learning is: a spam filter, step by step
lessons.summary: Learn machine learning with one example, a spam filter: training on examples, inference with a probability, and how the same idea routes alerts and spots unusual metrics.

lessons.title: AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI
lessons.summary: The big words, one at a time: artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, generative and predictive AI, and where you meet each one as a DevOps engineer.

lessons.title: Fix a 3 a.m. outage the classic way
lessons.summary: Follow an on-call engineer through a real nginx outage without any AI: reproduce it, read the logs and config, check the docs, fix it and update the runbook. Then do it yourself in the lab.

lessons.title: The same outage, fixed with an AI helper on Amazon Bedrock
lessons.summary: Replay the 3 a.m. 502 with an AI helper on Amazon Bedrock: what gets faster, what doesn't, and why the engineer still reviews every step. Then run it yourself in the lab.

lessons.title: Models: parameters, training, inference and model cards
lessons.summary: What an LLM is, parameters, pre-training, fine-tuning, inference, the knowledge cut-off, model cards, and open versus closed models: what to check before you deploy one.

lessons.title: Prompts, tokens, context windows and temperature
lessons.summary: The words every model call uses: prompt, system prompt, tokens, context window, temperature, max tokens, streaming and structured output, and how each changes the answer and the bill.

lessons.title: Hallucinations, grounding and judging AI answers
lessons.summary: Fluent is not correct. Learn hallucination, grounding, citations, groundedness, evaluation and the golden set, and how to measure whether an AI answer can be trusted.

lessons.title: Embeddings and vectors: matching meaning, not words
lessons.summary: How embeddings place similar meanings close together, what vectors, dimensions and similarity are, and why chunks and questions must use the same embedding model.

lessons.title: AI agents: tools, the agent loop, memory and guardrails
lessons.summary: A chatbot answers, an agent acts. Tools, function calling, MCP, the agent loop, memory, multiple agents, the human in the loop and guardrails, with the DevOps limits that keep agents safe.

lessons.title: AI chatbot versus AI agent, side by side
lessons.summary: Same model, same question: a chatbot that answers and an agent that acts. See how each works, what each can do, when to use which, and the guardrails an agent needs. Lab included.

lessons.title: What MCP is and why every platform adopted it
lessons.summary: The Model Context Protocol: the problem it solves, its three roles, why GitHub, AWS, Microsoft, Atlassian and Slack adopted it, and how an agent acts as a scoped delegate.

lessons.title: Your next step in AI-powered DevOps
lessons.summary: Where to go from here: the AWS and Azure masterclasses for building AI systems yourself, and the n8n course for automating your team's work, shown with real moments from their lessons.

lessons.title: Your next step: the AI for DevOps masterclasses on AWS and Azure
lessons.summary: What you can do now, and how the AWS and Azure masterclasses take you from these foundations to building, securing and running AI systems yourself.
lessons.articleMd:
You now speak the language of AI: what a model is, how you talk to it, why it sometimes makes things up, how embeddings match meaning, and what turns a chatbot into an agent. You have also seen a real outage fixed by hand and with an AI helper.

The next step is to build these systems yourself, on the cloud your team uses. That is what the two **AI for DevOps masterclasses** are for. Each one stands on its own: it starts with the full AI foundations, so nothing is missing if you join there, then goes much further, hands-on.

## AI for DevOps on AWS: From Fundamentals to Production
- **Build an AI chatbot on Amazon Bedrock** the DevOps way, with Terraform and least-privilege IAM.
- **Build a RAG system with Bedrock Knowledge Bases** that answers from your own documents, and run a production-style RAG stack with Docker Compose.
- **Put AI agents to work:** skill agents that fix 502 errors, crash loops and full disks, and an agent that diagnoses and repairs Kubernetes workloads, with your approval for every change.
- **Build your first MCP server** and connect real agents to it.
- **Automate with AI** in CI/CD and n8n workflows, then run AI in production: LLMOps, security and cost.

[See the AWS masterclass]({{course:ai-for-devops-aws}})

## AI for DevOps on Azure: From Fundamentals to Production
- **Deploy your first model in Microsoft Foundry** and ship a full-stack AI chat app on it.
- **Build a RAG system on Azure with Terraform** that answers from your own documents.
- **Put AI agents to work** on real DevOps problems: 502s, crash loops, full disks and broken Kubernetes workloads, always with a human approving.
- **Build your first MCP server**, connect agents to it, and automate with AI in CI/CD and n8n workflows.
- **Run AI like any other production service:** monitoring, security and cost.

[See the Azure masterclass]({{course:ai-for-devops-azure}})

## Which one is for you?
Choose the cloud your team runs on, or the one you want to work with next. Both teach the same AI skills; the hands-on labs use that cloud's own services. More lessons are being added to both, including AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry Agent Service, AI pull request reviews, guardrails and production deployments, and you get them as they are published.

Thank you for learning with DevOps Easy Learning.

## Automate it: AI-Powered DevOps Automation with n8n
If you would rather start by automating your team's work, the n8n course builds deployment notifications, Kubernetes alerts, incident workflows and AI summaries a human reviews.

[See the n8n course]({{course:n8n-automation}})
